name: Sleep-timed brain dose
subtitle: a nose spray fired at deep sleep

effects.effect: during deep sleep the brain flushes out waste through fluid channels
small molecules seep through a membrane

effect: during deep sleep the brain flushes out waste through fluid channels
how: Drugs meant for the brain mostly bounce off the barrier around its blood vessels, so doses have to be big and the side effects come with them. Only in deep sleep does fluid wash through the channels that wrap those vessels. A thin headband watches for the slow brain waves that mark that moment and tells a small nose pump to fire, so the dose arrives while the current is running.
obstacle: Nobody has shown that a dose timed to a slow wave actually reaches more brain than the same dose at bedtime.
why: Sleep-gated brain flushing is real; timing a dose to it is untested but cheap to try.
real: Searched for intranasal dosing timed to slow-wave sleep: the pieces are published separately (anesthesia-boosted nose-to-brain transport in rats; glymphatic flow tracking NREM slow waves; a WARF patent application on stimulus patterning plus real-time drug-delivery timing for brain clearance) but no device or study fires a nasal dose on detected slow-wave sleep.
